QF.id: XC Case Studies and Practical Application_5

question.text: Sunita, age 60, has just retired with Rs.2 crore. She needs Rs.75,000 per month for living expenses. She has no other income source. What allocation strategy would best serve her needs?

answer.text: 100% equity for maximum growth to sustain the corpus over 25+ years
A liquidity-and-stability approach: keep near-term income needs in liquid/short-term debt with maturities matched to the horizon, and retain some long-term growth/inflation-hedge exposure in equity
100% in bank fixed deposits for guaranteed safety
Invest entirely in high-yield corporate bonds for maximum income

explanation.text: The Logic: Series X-A supports retirement planning around expense adequacy and income stability in decumulation, matching debt maturity to the horizon, and retaining some long-term growth and inflation-hedge exposure. An SWP from the conservative portion can deliver the monthly income while equity preserves real value over a long retirement. The Trap: 100% equity is too volatile for a retiree with no other income. 100% FDs may not beat inflation over decades. High-yield corporate bonds carry credit risk unsuitable for a sole retirement corpus. Note: Precise bucket-year ranges (such as a 2-3 year and 3-7 year ladder) are illustrative and were not found in the checked X-A pages; the source-backed principle is liquidity and income stability with some long-term growth, not a specific ladder.
